By default the filter treats sexualised images of women and of men the same. If one of them simply isn\'t a temptation for you, you can turn it down — so you can shop for swimwear or underwear without a fight.\n\nThis only softens the SUGGESTIVE end. Explicit content and known adult sites stay blocked either way, whatever these switches say.
Locked while you\'re in %1$s mode.\nBoth are fully on. Switch to Relaxed to change them.
Bikinis, lingerie, cleavage and the like.
Health and medical pages are already treated differently — looking up a symptom is not the same as looking at porn, and the filter knows the difference.
Everything this app does to you, and exactly when. No surprises.
Even in Relaxed. Off is the one exception - see its card below.
You are in this mode right now
Strict lock is running: %1$s left. You cannot go back to Relaxed until it ends. You can still go up to Super hardcore.
One exception to everything below: OFF mode. In Off, monitoring is completely disabled and none of these rules run.
Known adult sites are blocked outright. Beyond Off, mode makes no difference.

Pages are scanned for sexual words. Every word carries a weight and they add up to a score - enough of them and the page is blocked, in every mode including Relaxed. No single word ever does it alone.
Anything on your ban list is blocked - the sites, pages, search terms and keywords you have banned yourself from.
Blocked browsers are covered the moment you open them. Only Firefox is left usable.
Dismiss a block on the same site enough times in one day and the whole site gets banned automatically for a while.
Short-form feeds (Reels, Shorts, TikTok-style) are blocked if you have that switch on.
Greylisted apps (TikTok, Instagram and friends) get %1$d minutes per hour, then they close.
\"Ride out the urge\" lockdown: %1$d minutes where only the essentials - calls, texts, alarms, maps - will open. It cannot be cancelled early.
Unlocking a relaxed window is limited: once a day, and only %1$d times ever.
There is no \"let me look anyway\" button. It is not on any screen, on purpose - a button like that is just a door with a handle, and sooner or later the urge tries the handle.

It IS still there, but you only get offered it if you go for the uninstall button, the device-admin lock, the monitoring switch, or try to escape a locked strict mode. Reach for the destructive option and you\'ll be offered the honest one instead - a wait, a written commitment, a fixed window, and everything still standing afterwards.
The app never presses Back for you. Blocking covers the screen and offers you the way out; it never navigates your browser behind your back.
A word-score block shows its working: the block screen lists the words that actually carried the score, so you can see why - and tell us when we got it wrong.

A web page needs a higher word score than an app screen before it is blocked, because in a browser the image add-on is reading the same page from the inside. One unmistakable word still blocks either, on its own.

Spelling it differently does not get past it. Numbers for letters, stretched letters, lookalike letters from other alphabets, and words split across spaces are all put back together before anything is checked.
Inside an APP, one unmistakable word is enough on a short screen - but the same word buried in a long page of text needs a second one, because a mention is not the same as a page about it.

…and even then, one detection does not close an app. Inside an app it opens a case instead: everything is then ignored for %1$d seconds, it takes a second detection after that, then another %2$d seconds ignored, then a third - %3$d separate looks before the app closes. The waits are the point. One question you typed, or one message somebody sent you, can never get past them.

How long that ladder is depends on how well the app is known. A NEW app - under %1$d days on the phone and not yet used on %2$d separate days - closes on the FIRST detection: a new install is exactly what looking for a way round a blocker looks like. An app we have already had to close for content gets %3$d. Everything else gets the full %4$d.

Nothing is held against you forever. %1$d minutes with no further detection in an app and its case is dropped unconfirmed; %2$d minutes with nothing detected in ANY app and every count everywhere goes back to zero.

string-array.name: mode_off_rules
string-array.item: Monitoring is OFF. Nothing is scanned and nothing is blocked - none of the \"Always on\" rules run in this mode.
This is the starting mode on a fresh install.
ONE-WAY DOOR: once you have EVER entered Strict, Off disappears for good. Relaxed becomes the loosest mode this install can reach.
The setup the blocker needs (page monitoring, the block screen, Firefox and its add-on) is OPTIONAL while you are here - the app never demands it.
Pick ANY other mode and both permissions become required: the app walks you through turning them on, and won\'t leave this screen until they are.
The Productivity page and its screen-time stats keep working either way.

string-array.name: mode_relaxed_rules
string-array.item: Greyscale: off. Your screen stays in colour.
Lying down or sitting in the dark changes nothing. Every app still opens - and no mode blocks on posture any more.
The \"who is the filter for\" switches (Adult content -> Settings) can be changed here (and in Off). In any stricter mode they are forced fully on.

Everything in \"Always on\" above still applies - blocking does not stop in Relaxed. Known adult sites, reddit (and every mirror/frontend of it), imageboards, a hand-picked borderline list and non-Google search engines are all still blocked here.
You can switch out of this mode whenever you like, unless the 7-day strict lock is running - but if you have ever been Strict, Off is no longer one of the choices.

string-array.name: mode_strict_rules
string-array.item: NIGHT GUARD: gone, in every mode. Lying down never blocks an app any more - not here, and not in Super hardcore. A dark room blocks nothing either.
ONE-WAY DOOR: picking Strict once removes Off from this install for good. You can drop back to Relaxed later - never to Off.

THE APP THAT KEEPS ALMOST BLOCKING: if a run of borderline words keeps coming up in one app for a few minutes, you get a warning screen saying so - and if it carries on, that app closes for an hour. Nothing here has crossed the line on its own; the pattern is the point. A clean stretch undoes it.

WHERE YOU LIVE: Strict asks you, once, to save where home is. Nothing in Strict acts on it - you are setting it up so it is ready if you ever go to Super hardcore, where being at home is what makes one word enough to close an app. It is GPS and nearby Wi-Fi, on this device only; nothing leaves the phone, and a VPN cannot move it. Set it up any time from Overview → Where you are.

THE HOUSE IS THEN FIXED. From here up, where you live is not a setting you can edit on a bad night - there is no way to move a saved house at all. You can ADD another one at any time, instantly, if you genuinely live in two places: that is always allowed, because being at home only ever makes the rules stricter. Removing one is asked for rather than done - it stays on for a while first, and you will not be told how long or when it finally goes.

ONE WORD STILL DOESN\'T CLOSE AN APP. Strict changes what counts as a detection - more word lists are live and the bar is lower - not how many it takes. It is the same ladder as every other mode: three separate detections for an app you have had a while, two for one we have closed before, one for a newly installed app.

THE SETUP IS ENFORCED, not just asked for: while anything is still missing - the \"appear on top\" permission, Firefox, or its add-on - everything except the essentials is covered with a screen naming the step you still owe. Calls, texts, alarms, maps, Settings, Firefox and this app all stay open, so you can always finish it (or drop back to Relaxed).
The \"who is the filter for\" switches are LOCKED fully on. You can only change those in Relaxed.
Greyscale: your screen turns grey while you are lying down.
Everything in \"Always on\" above still applies.
The 7-day strict lock (if you start it) stops you dropping back to Relaxed for a week. You can still go UP to Super hardcore.

string-array.name: mode_superhardcore_rules
string-array.item: NIGHT GUARD: gone. Lying down used to block everything but the essentials here - it no longer blocks anything, in any mode. A dark room does not block anything either.
Greyscale: your screen still turns grey while you are lying down, same as Strict. That is now the only thing posture changes.
Everything in \"Always on\" above still applies.
The borderline-pattern rule from Strict applies here too.

AT HOME, ONE WORD IS ENOUGH - only in this mode. When the phone can see it is at your house, the detection ladder collapses to one: the first sexual word detected in an app closes it, with no second look and no waiting to see whether it comes back. The house is where it happens, and this is the mode that says so.

Out of the house - or if it cannot tell where you are - the ordinary ladder applies: three separate detections, minutes apart. Being unsure NEVER makes anything stricter, so a vague fix in a supermarket cannot take an app away.
That rule needs the house saved first (Overview → Where you are). Until it is, Super hardcore uses the ordinary ladder everywhere.

THE HOUSE IS THEN FIXED. From here up, where you live is not a setting you can edit on a bad night - there is no way to move a saved house at all. You can ADD another one at any time, instantly, if you genuinely live in two places: that is always allowed, because being at home only ever makes the rules stricter. Removing one is asked for rather than done - it stays on for a while first, and you will not be told how long or when it finally goes.

Away from home the detection ladder is the same as everywhere else: one word in an app opens a case rather than closing the app. What this mode changes on top of that is what counts as a detection - the fragment lists (reddit and its misspellings) are only live here.
The setup is enforced outside this app exactly as it is in Strict: anything still missing and only the essentials open.
ONE-WAY DOOR: choosing this mode is permanent. Once it is on, no lower mode can ever be set again on this phone - Strict, Relaxed and Off all leave the picker for good.

How do I bring this down?
A rough model, not a medical measurement. It exists to make a pattern visible, nothing more.
Time is the biggest lever, by a mile.
Everything else in the score is small change next to how long you spend in the worst categories. An hour less short-form video will move this number more than a perfect day of everything else.
The first hour matters least, the fourth matters most.
The curve is deliberately steep at the top end. Cutting a four-hour day to three does more than cutting a one-hour day to zero.
Don\'t start the day in a feed.
Use just after waking is weighted harder, and it sets the tone for the whole day. Put the first unlock somewhere else.
Don\'t end it in one either.
Late-night use is weighted hardest of all, because you\'re paying twice: the hit, and the sleep.
Unlocks are a habit, not a need.
Most unlocks aren\'t for anything. The count itself is the signal - if it\'s high, you\'re reaching for it on autopilot.
A high interaction rate means thumbing a feed. A low one means reading something. The same hour can be either.
Get out of bed, and turn a light on.
Lying down in the dark with a phone is the single most reliable setup for a bad night. Nothing blocks on posture any more, so this one is on you - but it still costs you points here.

\nAnd the honest bit: this recovers slowly. The anti-rules in the score are weak on purpose, because a walk does not undo a four-hour binge and a number that pretended otherwise would be useless to you.
This is the one this whole app is built around. Everything on the Adult Content page - strict mode, the ban list, the night guard - is aimed at exactly this.
Short-form video is the most concentrated dose available to you. Turn on the short-form block (Temptations → Endless Scrolling) and the feeds die while the rest of the app still works.
Drop these to the grey tier so they get a few minutes an hour and then close. Temptations → Social Comparison has the switch.
Temptations → Impulse Shopping blocks the sites. The 48-hour basket rule does the rest.
Temptations → News Cycles. Pick one time a day to read it, and block it the rest of the time.
Less concentrated than the short stuff, but it eats whole evenings. Temptations → Binge Watching.
Temptations → Gaming & Reward Loops. Name what you\'re avoiding by playing.
This is the one category here that can take more than your time. If it\'s showing up at all, it\'s worth treating as seriously as the adult content.
Leave it in another room. Most of these aren\'t decisions - you won\'t miss what you never reached for.
You unlocked and were in a feed before you\'d thought about it. That\'s the purest autopilot there is. Moving the app off your home screen breaks the reflex more than willpower does.
Opening the same app over and over in an hour is a tic, not a use. The grey tier (a few minutes an hour, then it closes) is built for it.
A high rate means you\'re thumbing, not reading. Slowing down IS the intervention.
Phone use lying down is what costs you most here. No mode blocks it for you now - but Strict and Super hardcore both grey the screen while you are lying down, which takes most of the pull out of it.
Cut the time first. It outweighs everything else in the score.
Every rule below adds points to a daily total, capped at 100. Higher is worse. Nothing here is hidden from you.
Each category is worth points at a full dose. A \"full dose\" is %1$d hours or more in a day. Below that it scales up on a curve, so the fourth hour costs you more than the first.
Example: 2 hours of %1$s is half the maximum dose, which on the curve is about %2$d%% of %3$d points ≈ %4$d points.
Time spent between %1$d:00 and 0%2$d:00 is multiplied by %3$s — you pay twice, once for the hit and once for the sleep. Use in the first %4$d minutes after waking is multiplied by %5$s.
Nothing below %1$d an hour. Full points at %2$d an hour or more.
%1$d points each time you unlock the phone and are inside a feed within %2$d seconds. No decision happened there.
Based on the MOST times you opened any single app within one hour. Nothing below %1$s opens; full points at %2$s.
Interactions per minute of screen time. Nothing below %1$d/min (that\'s reading). Full points at %2$d/min (that\'s thumbing a feed).
Full points at %1$d hours of phone use lying down.
Full points at %1$d hours of phone use in a dark room.

Time with the screen off — up to %1$d points back, with full credit at %2$d waking hours off the phone.\n\nThat is deliberately small. A calm evening does not undo a four-hour binge, and a score that pretended it did would be no use to you.

Being straight with you about the holes:

• We cannot tell when you woke up. Android gives us no alarm signal, so we treat your first unlock after a %1$d+ hour gap as "just woke up". Nap and it'll misfire.

• Screen-off credit doesn't know whether a podcast is playing. Seeing that needs a permission this app deliberately doesn't take.
Pick how much time on the phone per day you\'d be happy with. The home-page graphs draw it as the dashed line. Until you set one, a 1-hour-a-day baseline is used.
Draws the target line on every usage graph
Two moves do most of the work: a real break away from your device, then locking it down hard for the week after. Everything else supports those two.
Get the troublesome ones out of easy reach.
Keep your phone out of the bedroom
Alarm clock so it never comes to bed - tap for the how.
Be out of the house as much as possible
Spend the money if you have to - on anything that isn\'t addictive. Friends and social clubs most of all.
Not just the apps - the accounts. Remove the pull entirely.
A clean visual reset every time you unlock.
Change your app theme, if you can
Make the phone feel like a different, less familiar device.
Go on holiday - without your device
Step right out of the environment the habit lives in. The single biggest reset.
Completed. You can run it again any time.
Do the holiday first - it\'s what protects the fresh start.
Lock yourself out for 7 days straight, right after the holiday.
Super-strict lock for a week after
Do the holiday first - it\'s what makes the lock stick.
More ways to keep the phone out of your hands.
The goal is simple: never need to bring your phone into the bedroom. If the phone isn\'t there at night, the highest-risk moments mostly disappear.
The single most important purchase. It removes the only honest reason to have the phone by your bed.
Charge your phone in another room
Pick a spot - kitchen, hallway - and make it the permanent overnight home for the phone.
So you never reach for the phone just to check the time.
Don\'t bring your phone to bed or high-risk spots
The bedroom, the bathroom, anywhere you\'ve slipped before. Leave it charging in another room.
Change your state when an urge hits
A shower, a cold blast at the end of it, a quick workout, stepping outside, a tight bedtime and wake-up routine, even a game - anything that breaks the moment and shifts how you feel.
Make the habit harder to reach by accident. Before anything else:
Move anything that tends to lead you in off your home screen - bury it in a folder, or remove the shortcut.
Sign out of accounts so opening them isn\'t one tap.
Delete the apps you don\'t truly need. The friction is the point.
Add the rest to this app\'s block list so they\'re handled for you.
Go on holiday / break the routine
The habit is wired to a place and a rhythm. The fastest way to weaken it is to physically leave that environment for a while.
Aim for a proper break - ideally around two weeks.
Go without your phone if you can, or leave it locked down the whole time.
Fill the days with people, movement and daylight - not screens.
Come back to a home you\'ve already rearranged, and start the 7-day lock fresh.
Strict mode stays on for 7 days. You can\'t switch back to relaxed until it ends. It\'s most effective once you\'ve reset with the holiday - you\'re protecting fresh ground, not fighting uphill.

resources.string: Break the comparison and validation loop.

string-array.name: temptspec_comparison_covers
string-array.item: Watching friends, influencers and peers post the highlight reel of their lives
FOMO - the sense that everyone else is somewhere better
Fishing for validation in likes, comments and views
Measuring your looks, money, job and progress against strangers
Coming away feeling behind, small, or quietly anxious

string-array.name: temptspec_checking_covers
string-array.item: Unlocking the phone with no idea why you picked it up
Checking notifications and messages purely out of reflex
Reaching for it the second you feel bored or uncomfortable
Doing it dozens of times a day without noticing
Wanting the choice back

string-array.name: temptspec_news_covers
string-array.item: Refreshing the news all day for an update that never settles anything
Reading the same bad story again and again, and doing nothing with it
Drowning in politics, disasters and problems you cannot personally touch
The loop: fear, uncertainty, check, brief relief, fear again
Being informed is fine. Being consumed by it is not.

string-array.name: temptspec_gaming_covers
string-array.item: Games built around streaks, unlocks, levels and daily rewards
Chasing progress that only exists inside the game
\"One more run\" turning into three hours
Playing to dodge boredom, stress, or something you owe someone
The point where entertainment quietly became a compulsion

string-array.name: temptspec_shopping_covers
string-array.item: Amazon, Temu, discount sites, ads following you around
Buying because you\'re bored, stressed, or high on getting a deal
\"Limited time\" offers engineered to stop you thinking
The hit is the ordering and the parcel - not the thing itself
Wanting to spend on purpose again
